oneLiner: Pro users can downgrade to Starter via self-service; the system computes prorated credit and schedules the change at billing cycle end.
requirementSummary: PROJ-1234 asks for self-service downgrade from Pro to Starter with prorated account credit applied at the end of the current billing cycle—not immediate plan swap or portal UI in this release.

integration.summary: Public API accepts downgrade requests, persists scheduled changes in Postgres, and an hourly worker applies them at cycle boundary; Stripe is read-only for subscription identity until the job runs; confirmation email uses the existing queue.

integration.mermaidSequence:
sequenceDiagram
  actor User as Pro tenant
  participant API as billing-api
  participant DB as Postgres
  participant Job as billing-jobs
  User->>API: POST downgrade + idempotency key
  API->>DB: insert row status=scheduled
  API-->>User: 202 pending_downgrade + credit preview
  Note over Job,DB: After effective_at (cycle end)
  Job->>DB: fetch due rows
  Job->>API: apply plan Starter
  Job->>DB: mark applied
  Job-->>User: confirmation email (once)

agentConsiderations.question: Use Stripe Schedule vs internal scheduling?
agentConsiderations.resolution: Internal table owns effective date because ledger credit is not modeled in Stripe Schedule.

agentConsiderations.question: Ship portal UI in same MR as API?
agentConsiderations.resolution: No—frontend capacity; AC4 deferred to PROJ-1290 with flag off until portal ready.

agentConsiderations.question: Timezone for cycle end?
agentConsiderations.resolution: Document UTC in API; human checklist flags product confirmation.

worthMentioning: Portal UI (AC4) is explicitly out of this MR—acceptable if PROJ-1290 is tracked.
Feature flag `billing.downgrade_self_service` stays off in prod until portal ships.

humanValidation.headline: You do not need to read every file—confirm the story matches AC1–AC3 and that AC4 deferral is acceptable for your release.
correctSignals: POST downgrade returns pending state and a credit amount tied to remaining cycle days—not an immediate Stripe plan change.
Row in `subscription_scheduled_changes` with `effective_at` at cycle boundary; worker applies only after that timestamp.
Repeat POST with same idempotency key does not double credit or create duplicate schedules.
OpenAPI documents UTC for cycle end; tests cover proration edge at month boundary.
redFlags: Stripe subscription price changes on API call instead of at job run.
No migration or index on `effective_at` while worker scans full table.
AC4 marked met without a tracked follow-up ticket.
Feature flag default `true` in production config.
